clue.text: Campanologists should be up to speed

definitions.text: Campanologists should be up to speed

parts.words: Campanologists should be up to speed
parts.note: bell-ringers handle ropes, so they should be familiar with them; the idiom for being experienced in a job is the same phrase

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers ought to be well practised before they perform.
explanation.walkthrough: Campanologists are bell-ringers, who pull ropes to sound church bells; the phrase meaning 'be experienced' is read literally for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be thoroughly familiar with how a job is done, which is being up to speed.

clue.text: Infringement of rules produces such ancillary effects

definitions.meaning: in rugby, a ... is the offence of knocking the ball forward with hand or arm
... effects are secondary consequences that follow on from something

explanation.surface: A breach of regulations has side effects.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a knock-on is knocking the ball forwards, which is against the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby uses the term for a handling offence, and as an adjective it describes consequential, secondary effects.

clue.text: Making love by sea with musicians —- it offers a gamble

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as the letter O
near means by or close to
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
a band is a group of musicians
taken as written

explanation.surface: Romancing beside the sea to music is something of a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a fruit machine, a coin-operated gambling machine with a lever on its side.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine with a side lever is a device that takes stakes, so it offers a gamble to players.

clue.text: Instruct cheat to reform

indicators.note: to reform the word cheat is to rearrange its letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: A tutor is told to set a cheating pupil straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: to instruct someone is to educate them in a subject.

clue.text: Say nothing, just drink

parts.note: to say something is to express it
nothing is zero, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: Keep quiet and simply have your drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a variant spelling of espresso, the strong coffee; 'just' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso, also spelt this way, is a strong black coffee and so a type of drink.

clue.text: Poet like Humpty-Dumpty heartless

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: Humpty-Dumpty is an egg in the nursery rhyme, and ovoid means egg-shaped

explanation.surface: A cruel poet is compared to the nursery-rhyme egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle O of OVOID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman writer of the Metamorphoses is a famous classical poet.

clue.text: Always hanging around behind New Englander, for instance

indicators.note: hanging around says the first piece is draped about the second, enclosing it

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
astern means behind, at the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone from New England keeps loitering at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging around' signals a container; 'behind' looks like position in the surface but is the nautical word for at the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: New England lies in the north-east of the USA, so a New Englander is an example of someone from the East.

clue.text: Exhausted? With a breather, fish will provide unlimited sport

parts.note: all in is an idiom for exhausted
a breather is a rest
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A worn-out angler takes a break and lands a catch fit for some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: All-in wrestling is a freestyle form with few restrictions on holds, hence 'unlimited'.
explanation.definitionFit: This freestyle form of grappling allows almost any hold, so it is a sport with few limits.

clue.text: A secretive person taken in by carpenter

definitions.meaning: someone who keeps things shut away, like a closed shell, is a clam-like person
in Lewis Carroll's poem The Walrus and the Carpenter, the pair trick shellfish into following them and eat them

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped man was fooled by a joiner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Walrus and the Carpenter, from Through the Looking-Glass, lure the shellfish along the beach and eat them.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-mouthed person is likened to a closed shellfish, and Carroll's carpenter deceives and eats such molluscs.

clue.text: Macbeth, say, works in Latin

definitions.meaning: Verdi wrote a version of Macbeth for the stage with singing
opus is Latin for a work, and its plural is the same as this word

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's play, perhaps, rendered in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: Verdi's Macbeth is a sung drama; in Latin the plural of opus (work) is this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Macbeth is an example of the art form, and the Latin plural of opus means works.

clue.text: Writer who discovered an element

definitions.meaning: J. B. ... wrote novels and plays such as An Inspector Calls
Joseph ..., an eighteenth-century chemist, isolated oxygen

explanation.surface: An author who also found a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: Two different men share the surname: the novelist J. B. and the chemist Joseph, who discovered oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the playwright of An Inspector Calls and to the chemist who identified oxygen.

clue.text: This covers head — king, queen, premier

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
premier means chief, first in rank

explanation.surface: A royal headscarf fit for king, queen and prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A square of cloth worn over the hair is a head covering.

clue.text: Son needs to be discriminatory

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A boy has to be prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating people unfairly on grounds of gender is a form of discrimination.

clue.text: Superfluous ruffles attached to front of shirt

parts.note: to ruffle someone is to irritate them, which is to needle them

indicators.note: front of says take the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Frills stitched to a shirt front are unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffles' looks like frills on a shirt but is the verb meaning annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superfluous is not required, i.e. unnecessary.

clue.text: House with shed in road leading to river

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a lane is a small road
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin
R is a map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A home with an outbuilding on a lane running down to the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like an outbuilding but is the verb; the House is the royal House of Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal dynasty of the Wars of the Roses was a noble house, in the sense of a family line.

clue.text: Some valetudinarians were fit

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A number of hypochondriacs were in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: Valetudinarians are people anxious about their health, which makes 'fit' look like part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit or suit a need is to serve it, as in 'that will serve the purpose'.

clue.text: Bird changed attire in high-performance car

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the car letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a fast touring car

indicators.note: changed says the letters of attire are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird in a new outfit drives a sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' signals the anagram and 'in' the container; GT (gran turismo) is the badge on a fast touring car.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common European songbird of the titmouse family.

clue.text: A pound — some capital in USA

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A pound gets you some money in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is the state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of New York State, so it is a state capital in America.

clue.text: Surprise attack made by a doctor on American husband

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
US abbreviates United States, so American

explanation.surface: A medic springs a surprise on the American's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack from a hidden position is a surprise assault, a waylaying.

clue.text: Interrupt endlessly, being disorderly and nastily obsessive

indicators.note: being disorderly says the letters are thrown into disorder
endlessly says the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A rowdy heckler keeps cutting in with unpleasant fixations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts INTERRUPT to INTERRUP, and 'being disorderly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prurient means having an unhealthy, excessive interest in sexual matters, an unpleasant obsession.

clue.text: This evening's hotting up

indicators.note: up here means stirred up, so the letters of hotting are disturbed

explanation.surface: The evening is getting warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', so the definition reads 'this evening is' before 'hotting up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means during the present evening or night.

clue.text: Boy meeting girl in Indian province once

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A romance blossoms in an old Indian province.
explanation.walkthrough: Bengal was a province of British India, now divided between India and Bangladesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The region was a province under British rule before partition, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Artists included a monk

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, so RAS are artists
to put in is to include

explanation.surface: Painters let a monk join them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'mad monk' Grigori Rasputin was a mystic at the court of the last Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was a Siberian holy man often called a monk.

clue.text: Rove bow line

parts.note: the bow of a ship is its prow

explanation.surface: Wander along the curve of a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam about stealthily, especially in search of prey, is to rove.

clue.text: Close and intimate

definitions.meaning: close can ... stingy, unwilling to spend
to intimate is to imply or signify

explanation.surface: Near and dear.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions use a different sense than the surface: close as tight-fisted, intimate as a verb meaning to suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means miserly (close) and also to signify or imply (intimate).

clue.text: Most annoyed, discovering garment without its accessories

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the garment surrounds the accessories

parts.note: a shirt is a garment
ties are clothing accessories

explanation.surface: Someone is furious on finding a shirt delivered with no extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. Shirty is British slang for annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirty is informal British for bad-tempered, so the superlative means the most irritated.

clue.text: Due to be successful in return game

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
return says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: go is a Japanese board game
to be successful is to win

explanation.surface: Ready to triumph in the rematch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the board game and 'in' holds the victory inside; 'return game' looks like a rematch in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that is outstanding is owed, i.e. payable or due.

clue.text: Reveal British girl, 19, has been converted

indicators.note: converted says the letters are changed into a new form

parts.note: the answer to 19 down

explanation.surface: A British girl has been won over this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been converted' signals an anagram of the girl together with the 19-down answer, a cross-reference rather than a number.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose or disclose something hidden is to reveal it.
